notes: Single source of truth for every configurable parameter. The API serves this at /api/v1/generation/schema; the frontend renders forms from it. 'kind' separates model generation parameters from ComfyUI workflow execution parameters and from post-processing. 'native' records whether the native YuE2 runtime has a true equivalent; unsupported parameters are disabled in the UI with the stated reason rather than silently ignored.

groups.label: Model
groups.description: Which weights and runtime back the generation.

groups.label: Planning
groups.description: Symbolic ABC plan written before any audio.

groups.label: Generation
groups.description: Acoustic token sampling, seed and duration budget.

parameters.label: Style
parameters.help: Genre, instruments, vocal character, language and tempo. Example: 'Cinematic Bengali folk-pop, warm male vocal, acoustic guitar, bamboo flute, organic drums, melancholic but hopeful, 92 BPM'.

guidance.what: The brief for the music: genre, instruments, the kind of voice, the language and the tempo. This is the single strongest influence on what you get back.
guidance.more: A richer description with instruments and a tempo gives the model much more to work with.
guidance.less: A bare description such as 'pop' leaves almost every decision to the model, so results vary wildly between runs.
guidance.recommended: One or two lines. Name the genre, two or three instruments, the vocal character and a BPM.

parameters.label: Lyrics
parameters.help: The words to sing. Use section tags on their own line: [Intro], [Verse], [Pre-Chorus], [Chorus], [Bridge], [Outro].

guidance.what: The words to be sung, with section tags such as [Verse] and [Chorus] on their own lines. The tags tell the model where the song's structure changes.
guidance.more: More sections give a longer, more structured song, up to the duration ceiling.
guidance.less: Very short lyrics tend to produce a short song, or repeated material to fill the time.
guidance.recommended: Use the section tags the model was trained on. Inventing new tag names does not create new behaviour.
guidance.cost: Very long lyrics crowd the context window and can lead to a truncated plan.

options.label: Full Song
options.help: Plan melody and chords as ABC, then generate audio.

options.label: Melody Guided
options.help: Plan melody only, leaving the accompaniment freer.

options.label: Direct Audio
options.help: Generate audio with no symbolic plan.

options.label: Cover
options.help: Condition on a melody transcribed from reference audio.

options.label: Score Edit
options.help: Regenerate from an ABC score you edited.

guidance.what: How much of the composition the model plans before it sings a note. Full Song writes a chord-annotated score first; Melody Guided writes only a melody; Direct Audio skips planning entirely; Cover transcribes a recording you supply; Score Edit regenerates from a score you edited.
guidance.more: Planning modes give more coherent structure and give you an editable score afterwards.
guidance.less: Direct Audio is quicker and less structured, and produces no score to edit.
guidance.recommended: Full Song unless you have a reason to do otherwise.
guidance.cost: Planning adds roughly ten seconds before audio generation begins.

parameters.label: ABC score
parameters.help: External composition used directly instead of a generated plan. Requires Full Song or Melody Guided; the native melody input has Vocal and Ins voices and no chord symbols.

guidance.what: A composition in ABC notation used instead of one the model writes. The model performs this material rather than inventing its own.
guidance.more: Supplying a score gives you exact control over melody and harmony.
guidance.less: Leaving it empty lets the model compose freely.
guidance.recommended: Leave empty unless you are editing a score the model produced.
guidance.extremes: The dialect is narrow: native X:1, a blank T: header, two voices named Vocal and Ins, and chord symbols on Vocal only. Anything else is refused with the parser's reason.
guidance.cost: Skips the planning stage, so a run is slightly faster.

parameters.label: Reference audio
parameters.help: The recording a cover is based on. It is transcribed to a melody score, which then guides generation.

native.note: Transcribed by the SheetSage2 service, then supplied to YuE2 as the planner input.

comfy.note: The workflow reads a file from ComfyUI's input directory; the studio uses an upload.

guidance.what: The recording a cover is based on. It is transcribed into a melody score, which then guides generation in your chosen style.
guidance.recommended: A clear recording with a prominent melody transcribes best.
guidance.extremes: Transcription is not exact. A dense or noisy mix transcribes poorly, and those errors carry straight into the cover. Review the score before you rely on the result.
guidance.cost: Transcription adds a separate pass on the GPU before generation starts.

parameters.label: Model
parameters.help: Local YuE2 model directory. Leave on the default to use the path from .env.

comfy.note: ComfyUI packages the model as a single .safetensors checkpoint; the native runtime loads a model directory.

guidance.what: Which set of model weights to generate with. Different checkpoints are trained or quantised differently, so they sound different and can need different amounts of VRAM.
guidance.recommended: Leave on Default unless you have deliberately installed another checkpoint.
guidance.extremes: Selecting a model whose files are missing fails the run immediately rather than falling back to another one.
guidance.cost: Switching models mid-session unloads the resident weights and reloads about 7 GB, which costs several seconds on the next run.

parameters.label: Model revision
parameters.help: Pin a Hugging Face revision for comparisons. Ignored when the model is a local directory.

guidance.what: Pins a specific published version of the model when it is fetched from Hugging Face, so a comparison months apart uses identical weights.
guidance.recommended: Leave empty. It has no effect on a local model directory, where the file hashes recorded in each manifest are the identity.

options.label: YuE2-Vae (listening)
options.help: Default decoder for generation and listening.

comfy.note: The workflow takes the VAE from the same checkpoint.

guidance.what: The decoder that turns the model's internal representation into audio you can hear. The standard decoder is tuned for listening; the legacy one exists to reproduce the published benchmark numbers.
guidance.recommended: Standard, unless you are reproducing a benchmark.

parameters.label: Decoder revision
parameters.help: Pin the decoder revision for comparisons.

guidance.what: Pins a published version of the decoder, for the same reason as the model revision.
guidance.recommended: Leave empty.

parameters.label: Compute backend
parameters.help: Autoregressive decoding backend. vLLM needs the optional 'fast' extras.

guidance.what: How the model's token generation is executed. Torch with CUDA graphs is the fast default; eager mode is slower but easier to debug; vLLM is an optional high-throughput path.
guidance.recommended: Torch.
guidance.extremes: Eager mode is noticeably slower. vLLM needs extra packages installed in the worker environment, and the option stays disabled until they are.

parameters.label: Quantization
parameters.help: With 48 GB of VRAM the unquantized preset is the quality default.

comfy.note: ComfyUI selects precision by choosing a different checkpoint file, e.g. yue2_convrot_int8.safetensors.

guidance.what: Whether the weights are compressed to a smaller numeric format before running. Compression saves memory at some cost to fidelity.
guidance.more: FP8 lowers VRAM use on hardware that supports it.
guidance.less: None keeps full bf16 precision and is the quality default.
guidance.recommended: None. With 48 GB there is no need to compress.
guidance.extremes: FP8 needs a GPU with compute capability 8.9 or newer; on older cards the option is disabled rather than silently ignored.
guidance.cost: Lowers VRAM; may slightly change how the output sounds.

parameters.label: Offload AR weights during synthesis
parameters.help: Moves the autoregressive weights off the GPU while latents are synthesised. Slower, but lowers the memory peak.

guidance.what: Moves the text-and-planning half of the model off the GPU while audio is being synthesised, freeing memory for the part that is actually working.
guidance.more: Turning it on lowers the peak VRAM a run needs.
guidance.less: Leaving it off keeps everything resident and is faster.
guidance.recommended: Off, unless you are sharing the GPU or hitting out-of-memory errors.
guidance.cost: Adds time to every run because weights move between GPU and system memory.

parameters.label: GPU memory budget (GiB)
parameters.help: Caps this process's GPU allocation and selects decoder chunking. The documented baseline is 24; an RTX A6000 has 48.

guidance.what: How much GPU memory this application is allowed to reserve. It also decides how large the decoder's chunks are.
guidance.more: A larger budget allows longer songs and faster whole-song decoding.
guidance.less: A smaller budget leaves room for other programs using the same GPU.
guidance.recommended: 24 is the documented baseline. 40 suits a 48 GB card that is not shared.
guidance.extremes: Setting it near the card's total leaves nothing for other processes; setting it very low forces small decoder chunks and slow decoding.
guidance.cost: Directly caps VRAM; too low a value causes out-of-memory failures on long songs.

parameters.label: Offline (local files only)
parameters.help: Never contact Hugging Face during a generation.

guidance.what: Forbids the application from contacting Hugging Face while generating. Everything must already be on disk.
guidance.recommended: On. It makes runs deterministic and keeps the machine offline.
guidance.extremes: With it off and a model that is not downloaded yet, the first run stalls while several gigabytes are fetched.
guidance.cost: None when the weights are already local.

parameters.label: Planner temperature
parameters.help: Randomness while writing the ABC plan. Lower keeps the composition conventional.

comfy.note: Not exposed as a widget in the reference workflow.

guidance.what: How adventurous the model is while writing the score, before any audio exists.
guidance.more: Higher values produce more unusual melodies and chord choices.
guidance.less: Lower values produce conventional, predictable composition.
guidance.recommended: 0.7. The planner is deliberately steadier than the audio stage.
guidance.extremes: Above about 1.5 the score often stops making musical sense, which then spoils the audio built on it.

parameters.label: Planner top-p
parameters.help: Nucleus sampling cutoff for the plan.

guidance.what: Limits the planner's choices to the most likely options that together account for this share of the probability.
guidance.more: Closer to 1 allows rarer musical ideas.
guidance.less: Lower values keep the composition safe and repetitive.

parameters.label: Planner top-k
parameters.help: Number of candidate tokens considered for the plan.

guidance.what: A hard cap on how many candidate notes or chords the planner weighs at each step.
guidance.more: Higher values widen the pool and add variety.
guidance.less: Lower values narrow it toward the single most obvious choice.
guidance.extremes: A value of 1 makes the planner fully deterministic and usually dull.

parameters.label: Planner repetition penalty
parameters.help: Discourages repeated bars. Scores repeat by design, so the default is nearly neutral.

guidance.what: Discourages the planner from writing the same bars over and over.
guidance.more: Higher values push harder against repeated material.
guidance.less: Lower values allow more repetition.
guidance.recommended: 1.005, which is almost neutral on purpose — real songs repeat their sections, and penalising that hurts structure.
guidance.extremes: Values much above 1.05 tend to destroy verse and chorus repetition, producing a score that wanders.

parameters.label: Planner penalty window
parameters.help: How many recent tokens the repetition penalty looks at.

guidance.what: How far back the repetition penalty looks when deciding whether something is a repeat.
guidance.more: A larger window catches repetition across longer spans.
guidance.less: A smaller window only notices immediate repeats.

parameters.label: Planner minimum tokens
parameters.help: Stops the plan from ending immediately.

guidance.what: A floor that stops the planner from ending the score almost immediately.
guidance.more: Higher values force a longer composition.
guidance.less: Lower values let the planner stop early.

parameters.label: ABC max tokens
parameters.help: Ceiling on plan length. Hitting it marks the result truncated rather than failing.

guidance.what: The longest score the planner may write. It is a ceiling, not a target.
guidance.more: A higher ceiling allows longer and more detailed compositions.
guidance.less: A lower ceiling cuts the score off, and a truncated score usually means the song ends abruptly.
guidance.extremes: If the planner reaches this limit the result is marked truncated and the warning says so; it does not fail.
guidance.cost: A longer score adds planning time before audio generation starts.

parameters.label: Planner seed
parameters.help: Separate seed for the planning stage.

native.note: The native pipeline derives both the plan and the acoustic tokens from one request seed (yue2.protocol.SongRequest.seed). Use Generation seed instead.

guidance.what: A separate random seed for the planning stage. This exists in the ComfyUI workflow only.
guidance.recommended: Not applicable here. The native runtime derives both the score and the audio from the single Seed below, so there is nothing separate to set.

parameters.label: Seed
parameters.help: The same seed with the same settings and the same weights reproduces a generation.

guidance.what: The starting point for every random choice in a run. The same seed with the same settings and the same weights reproduces the same song.
guidance.more: Any different number gives a completely different take on the same brief.
guidance.recommended: Keep a seed you like, and change one setting at a time to hear what that setting does.

parameters.label: Seed behaviour

options.label: Randomize
options.help: Draw a new seed on the server for each run and record it.

options.label: Increment
options.help: Add one to the seed after each run.

parameters.help: Applied by the studio before the request reaches the model. The seed actually used is always saved to the manifest.

native.note: Resolved by the studio; the runtime only ever sees a concrete seed.

guidance.what: What happens to the seed after a run. Fixed reuses it, Randomize draws a fresh one on the server, Increment adds one.
guidance.recommended: Randomize while you are exploring, then switch to Fixed once you find a take worth refining.
guidance.extremes: The seed actually used is always saved to the manifest, so a randomised take is never lost.

parameters.label: Temperature
parameters.help: Randomness of the acoustic tokens. Higher is more adventurous and less stable.

guidance.what: How adventurous the model is while generating the audio itself. This is the main creativity dial.
guidance.more: Higher values give more variation and surprise, and less stability.
guidance.less: Lower values give consistent, conservative performances.
guidance.extremes: Much above 1.5 the performance tends to drift, lose the beat, or produce noise. Near 0 it becomes flat and repetitive.

parameters.label: Top-p
parameters.help: Keeps only the most likely tokens that together reach this probability.

guidance.what: Keeps only the most likely sounds that together account for this share of the probability, and ignores the long tail.
guidance.more: Closer to 1 keeps rarer choices in play, adding variety and risk.
guidance.less: Lower values tighten the performance toward the safest option.

parameters.label: Top-k
parameters.help: Hard cap on how many candidate tokens are considered at each step.

guidance.what: A hard cap on how many candidate sounds the model weighs at each step.
guidance.more: Higher values widen the pool.
guidance.less: Lower values narrow it.
guidance.recommended: 100. Top-p usually does the useful work; this is a backstop.

parameters.label: Repetition penalty
parameters.help: Pushes the model away from looping the same material.

guidance.what: Pushes the model away from looping the same musical material.
guidance.more: Higher values break loops more aggressively.
guidance.less: Lower values allow more repetition, which can turn into a stuck groove.
guidance.extremes: Above roughly 1.5 the performance becomes restless and can lose its groove, because a steady beat is itself repetition.

parameters.label: Penalty window
parameters.help: How many recent acoustic tokens the repetition penalty considers.

guidance.what: How many recent moments the repetition penalty considers when judging a repeat.
guidance.more: A larger window notices repetition across longer stretches.
guidance.less: A smaller window only reacts to immediate loops.

parameters.label: Minimum tokens
parameters.help: Floor on song length: 25 tokens is one second of audio, so 200 is eight seconds.

guidance.what: A floor on song length. Twenty-five units is one second, so 200 is about eight seconds.
guidance.more: Higher values stop the model from finishing too early.
guidance.less: Lower values let a short idea end when it wants to.

parameters.label: Maximum duration
parameters.help: Upper bound on song length. The model stops when the song is finished, so a longer limit does not force a longer song. One second is 25 acoustic tokens.

native.note: Converted to tokens with the VAE's 25 frames per second (sample_rate 48000 / downsampling_ratio 1920).

guidance.what: The longest the song is allowed to be. The model stops when the song feels finished, so this is a ceiling rather than a target.
guidance.more: A higher ceiling lets a long song finish instead of being cut off.
guidance.less: A lower ceiling keeps runs short while you are experimenting.
guidance.recommended: Two to three minutes for a full song; 30 to 60 seconds while trying ideas.
guidance.extremes: If the model reaches the ceiling the result is marked truncated and may end abruptly. Long songs are also where GPU memory runs out.
guidance.cost: This is the single biggest influence on both generation time and VRAM. Roughly, time scales with the audio produced.

parameters.label: Semantic max tokens (override)
parameters.help: Set the token ceiling directly instead of deriving it from the duration. Leave empty to use Maximum duration.

guidance.what: Sets the length ceiling directly in model units instead of in seconds. Twenty-five units is one second of audio.
guidance.recommended: Leave empty and use Maximum duration, which is the same control in friendlier units.
guidance.extremes: A value here overrides the duration slider entirely, so the two can appear to disagree.

parameters.label: Guidance (CFG)
parameters.help: How strongly the text and score steer the audio. Empty uses the runtime default: 1.0 with a plan, 1.01 without one.

guidance.what: How strongly the style, lyrics and score are allowed to steer the audio, as opposed to letting the model follow its own instincts.
guidance.more: Higher values follow your brief more literally, at the cost of naturalness.
guidance.less: Lower values give the model more freedom and a looser reading of the brief.
guidance.recommended: Leave empty to use the runtime default, which is 1.0 with a plan and 1.01 without one.
guidance.extremes: Large values tend to produce strained, over-constrained audio.
guidance.cost: Values other than 1.0 run a second guidance pass, which makes generation slower.

parameters.label: Synthesis steps
parameters.help: Solver steps used to turn acoustic tokens into latents. More steps cost time; the default is the validated setting.

guidance.what: How many refinement steps are used to turn the model's internal representation into detailed audio. Think of it as how many passes the renderer makes.
guidance.more: More steps can give slightly cleaner detail.
guidance.less: Fewer steps are faster and rougher.
guidance.recommended: 32, which is the validated setting. Gains above it are small.
guidance.extremes: Very low values produce audible artefacts.
guidance.cost: Time scales almost linearly with this number; doubling it roughly doubles the synthesis stage.

parameters.label: Solver
parameters.help: Fixed by the runtime protocol at this context length.

comfy.note: ComfyUI's sampler list is a different mechanism and does not map onto this.

guidance.what: The mathematical recipe used to take each refinement step. Different recipes trade accuracy against the number of steps needed; this runtime is built and validated around one of them.
guidance.recommended: Fixed by the runtime. It cannot be changed at this context length, and is shown so the synthesis settings are complete.

parameters.label: Sampler
parameters.help: ComfyUI KSampler sampler.

native.note: The native runtime solves the flow-matching ODE with a fixed midpoint solver and has no sampler list. Use Synthesis steps instead.

guidance.what: In ComfyUI, the algorithm that walks from noise to a finished result. Different samplers take different paths and sound slightly different.
guidance.recommended: Not applicable here. This runtime uses one fixed solver, so there is no sampler list to choose from; use Synthesis steps instead.

parameters.label: Scheduler
parameters.help: ComfyUI KSampler noise schedule.

native.note: No native equivalent: the solver uses a uniform midpoint schedule.

guidance.what: In ComfyUI, how the refinement steps are spaced out — evenly, or concentrated at one end.
guidance.recommended: Not applicable here. The spacing is uniform and not configurable.

parameters.label: Denoise
parameters.help: ComfyUI partial-denoise strength.

native.note: The native pipeline always solves the full trajectory; there is no partial-denoise entry point.

guidance.what: In ComfyUI, how much of the existing content is replaced rather than kept, which is how image-to-image style workflows work.
guidance.recommended: Not applicable here. This runtime always renders the full trajectory, so there is no partial-refinement entry point.

parameters.label: Latent length (seconds)
parameters.help: ComfyUI allocates an empty latent of this length before sampling.

native.note: The native pipeline sizes latents from the acoustic tokens the model actually emitted, so there is nothing to preallocate. Use Maximum duration.

guidance.what: In ComfyUI, the length of the empty audio canvas reserved before generation begins, which fixes the maximum length of the result.
guidance.recommended: Not applicable here. This runtime sizes its canvas from the audio the model actually produced. Use Maximum duration.

parameters.label: Batch size
parameters.help: ComfyUI latent batch size.

native.note: One pipeline call produces one candidate. Queue several generations to get variations.

guidance.what: In ComfyUI, how many separate results a single run produces, so several variations come back together.
guidance.recommended: Not applicable here. One run produces one song; queue several runs to compare takes.

parameters.label: Decoder mode

options.label: Tiled
options.help: Decodes in chunks. Predictable memory, works at any length.

options.label: Whole song
options.help: Decodes in one pass. Faster when VRAM allows; can run out of memory on long songs.

parameters.help: The reference workflow notes that regular decoding is faster when there is enough VRAM. It is not guaranteed to fit at every duration.

comfy.note: ComfyUI models this as two separate nodes, VAEDecodeAudio and VAEDecodeAudioTiled.

guidance.what: How the finished song is turned into an audio file: all at once, or in chunks that are stitched together.
guidance.more: Whole-song decoding is faster when there is enough free GPU memory.
guidance.less: Tiled decoding uses a predictable, much smaller amount of memory and works at any length.
guidance.recommended: Tiled. It is the safe choice and the speed difference is small.
guidance.extremes: Whole-song decoding of a long track is the most common cause of out-of-memory failures.
guidance.cost: Whole-song is faster but its memory use grows with song length.

parameters.label: Tile size (latent frames)
parameters.help: Latent frames decoded per chunk; 25 frames is one second. Smaller tiles use less memory and take longer.

comfy.note: The workflow's 1920 is the VAE downsampling ratio, not this frame count.

guidance.what: How much audio the tiled decoder handles per chunk. Twenty-five frames is one second.
guidance.more: Larger chunks decode faster and use more memory.
guidance.less: Smaller chunks use less memory and take longer.
guidance.recommended: 1024, or 512 if you are sharing the GPU.
guidance.extremes: Very small tiles make decoding noticeably slow; very large ones defeat the purpose of tiling.
guidance.cost: Directly trades decoding time against VRAM.

parameters.label: Tile overlap (latent frames)
parameters.help: Context decoded either side of each tile and then cropped. Fixed by the runtime.

guidance.what: A little extra audio decoded either side of each chunk and then trimmed off, so the joins between chunks are inaudible.
guidance.recommended: Fixed by the runtime. It is shown so the decoder settings are complete, not because you need to change it.

parameters.label: Format

options.label: FLAC (24-bit)
options.help: The runtime's own lossless output. No re-encoding.

options.label: MP3
options.help: Converted from the canonical FLAC with FFmpeg after generation.

parameters.help: FLAC and WAV are written by the model runtime. MP3 is an explicit post-processing conversion and keeps the lossless file alongside it.

guidance.what: The file you get. FLAC and WAV are lossless and are written directly by the model runtime. MP3 is smaller and is converted from the lossless file afterwards.
guidance.recommended: FLAC. It is lossless, widely supported and about half the size of WAV.
guidance.extremes: MP3 loses a little quality by design, and requires FFmpeg to be installed. The lossless master is always kept alongside it.
guidance.cost: MP3 adds a second or two of conversion after generation.

parameters.label: Filename prefix
parameters.help: Prefix for downloaded files. Artifact paths on disk are derived from ids and do not change.

native.note: Applied by the studio when a file is downloaded.

guidance.what: The start of the filename when you download a song. Files on disk are named from internal ids and are unaffected.
guidance.recommended: Anything recognisable, such as a project name.

parameters.label: Keep the lossless master
parameters.help: The model's own output is always retained untouched as the canonical artifact.

guidance.what: Keeps the model's own untouched output alongside any converted copy, so nothing you generate is ever only available in a lossy format.
guidance.recommended: Always on; it is not something you should need to turn off.
